title: Score a day of card payments on every core

blocks.text: The card team scores every payment of the day for fraud risk and adds up the points. Scoring one amount is pure arithmetic, but a busy day has forty million of them, and on one thread the nightly job no longer finishes before the morning settlement run. The job has been given a `ForkJoinPool`, and `RiskPoints` already wraps the day in one task and hands it to that pool.
Finish `compute()` of the `Total` task in `src/main/java/practice/RiskPoints.java`. When you're done:

items: the total is right for any day, including an empty one;
the pool's workers score the day together, rather than one after another;
the operations dashboard, which shows `tasksCreated()`, sees a few tasks per `threshold` amounts, not one per payment. A range of exactly `threshold` amounts is one task.

blocks.text: About ten lines in total. The tests run `RiskPoints` on real pools of two and three workers.

cases.says: the total is the sum of the points of every amount, for empty, short and long days and any threshold
a range no longer than the threshold is scored by its own task without creating more, so the number of tasks stays in proportion to amounts divided by threshold
the two halves of a range that is split are scored at the same time, on two workers

origin.section: The Threshold Decides Whether Splitting Pays

concepts: A fork/join task forks one half, computes the other on its own thread, then joins; joining before computing gives the right result at the speed of one thread.
The threshold decides how many tasks there are: a task per element costs more than the work it wraps, one task gives no parallelism, and a wide range in between performs alike when work is even.
